objective: Finish the Factory throughput overhaul. VERIFIED BASELINE (production, 2026-10-30) — extend these owners, never add a second scheduler, queue or router beside them. Already landed by hand as the bootstrap (PR factory/parallel-units): server/services/factory/remoteLoop.ts runRemoteTick now creates one FACTORY_UNITS bin per READY unit via createUnitsBin(campaign, cr, [unit]) and uses liveUnitKeys()/unitKeysOfBin() from server/services/factory/remote.ts so no unit is handed out twice, and lets the integration stage start while sibling units are still with workers; createPlanBin tells the planner to shape wide, shallow graphs. Measured before it: campaign fcp_0b8d9fccd0064270ae34 waited 2h07m from plan bin created (00:55:49Z) to plan installed (03:02:53Z) and four live campaigns each had exactly one unit with the fleet while every dispatch read FLEET_TARGET_REACHED. What remains, as four independent pieces of work: (1) CROSS-CAMPAIGN CONFLICTS BY REAL OWNERSHIP. server/services/factory/line.ts admitQueued holds a queued objective whenever its declared mutationScope pathsOverlap()s any live campaign's scope, so broad scopes such as 'tests/**' or 'server/db/migrations/**' serialize unrelated campaigns. Replace that comparison with one against the ownedPaths of the other live campaigns' units that are not INTEGRATED, CANCELLED or FAILED (a campaign with no units yet blocks nothing), and in remoteLoop.ts, before creating a unit's bin, defer only that unit (with a stageDetail/note naming the other campaign and unit) when its ownedPaths pathsOverlap() a LEASED, IMPLEMENTED or bin-carried READY unit of another live campaign in the same repository; independent units of the same campaign keep going. Directly approved campaigns (scripts/factory.ts approve) get the same unit-level protection because it lives in the tick. (2) OWNER-LAST ROUTING. Add 'RESERVE' to FLEET_ACCOUNT_KINDS in server/domain/types.ts; in server/services/dispatch/router.ts routeBin rank a RESERVE account's Routine after every eligible non-RESERVE Routine (before delivery standing, allowance and headroom ordering) and append to the selection reason that the reserve account was used and why (no non-reserve surface was eligible, with the refusals); never make RESERVE ineligible. Add a `set-kind --kind account --ref <name> --to CAPACITY|RESERVE --reason <text>` command to scripts/fleet.ts writing through a new guarded repo function in server/repos/fleet.ts, recorded the way set-state records an operator decision; `fleet show` prints each account's kind. (3) STAGE LATENCY MEASUREMENTS. Extend server/services/factory/throughput.ts ThroughputReport with a `stages` block computed from the campaign's own bins and factory events: planDurationMs (plan bin created to PLAN_INSTALLED), timeToFirstCodingMs (campaign created to the first FACTORY_UNITS bin's first lease), per-stage queue delay (bin READY to first lease, from bins/bin_events, per kind: average and max), integrationDelayMs and reviewDelayMs (UNIT_IMPLEMENTED to the integrate bin's lease; integrated head to review bin lease), concurrentUnitBinsMax (peak simultaneously LEASED FACTORY_UNITS bins), unitsPerHour and completionMs; each an EvidenceNumber, null with basis 'not measured' when the rows do not exist, never 0. Print the block in scripts/factory.ts `throughput`. (4) IDLE REASONS. In scripts/factory.ts add `idle` printing, for every READY factory bin, how long it has waited and its current dispatch lastErrorKind/reason (e.g. FLEET_TARGET_REACHED with in-flight and target), and for every routable Routine whether it is in flight, rate limited until when, quarantined, or idle, using the existing fleetSnapshot()/routeBin() readings rather than re-deriving eligibility.
expectedOutcome: Unrelated campaigns no longer wait on each other's broad declared scopes, only on real overlapping unit ownership; a RESERVE account is fired only when no other eligible surface can take the bin and the reason says so; `factory throughput` reports measured planning, first-coding, queue, integration and review latencies and peak concurrent implementation bins; `factory idle` explains every waiting bin and idle surface.
nonGoals: Implementing any of the five queued Brain upgrade objectives
Changing credentials, secrets, account permissions, authorization, server/services/identity/**, server/services/bins/routing.ts or any repository envelope
Raising or lowering fleet, account or Routine targets in code, or ignoring a provider refusal or retry window
Bypassing independent review, forge verification, integration verification, delivery checks or the release gate
A second scheduler, queue, router or metrics store beside the existing ones

acceptanceConditions.statement: tests/factoryCrossCampaign.test.ts: two queued objectives whose declared scopes both include 'tests/**' but whose live units own disjoint files are both admitted by admitQueued; one whose queued scope overlaps a live, unintegrated unit's ownedPaths is held with a reason naming that campaign.

tests/factoryCrossCampaign.test.ts: a READY unit whose ownedPaths overlap a LEASED or IMPLEMENTED unit of another live campaign in the same repository gets no bin on the tick and the campaign's note names the other unit, while a disjoint sibling in the same campaign does get a bin; once the other unit is INTEGRATED the deferred unit gets its bin on the next tick.

tests/fleetReserveRouting.test.ts: routeBin chooses an eligible CAPACITY Routine over an eligible RESERVE Routine even when the RESERVE one has more headroom, chooses the RESERVE one when it is the only eligible surface and its reason says the reserve account was used, and never refuses a bin because its only surface is RESERVE.

tests/factoryStageLatency.test.ts: for a campaign built from rows with known timestamps the throughput report's stages block returns the exact planDurationMs, timeToFirstCodingMs, queue delays and concurrentUnitBinsMax; a stage with no rows reports value null with a basis, never 0.

scripts/factory.ts has an `idle` command and `throughput` prints the stages block; scripts/fleet.ts has `set-kind` and `show` prints account kind; tests cover the set-kind repo function refusing an unknown kind.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the merged pull request. No migration: account kind is an existing TEXT column, so a RESERVE row reverts to being routed like any account and nothing is deleted.
